description: A column's DEFAULT (and AUTOINCREMENT) applies only when the column is OMITTED from an INSERT - a column explicitly listed keeps its value, including an explicit NULL, whether from VALUES, a SELECT source, a positional row or a MERGE insert; omitted columns still take their defaults everywhere. Converted 1:1 from dml/InsertExplicitNullVsDefaultTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR DEFAULT 'NA', score NUMBER(5,3) DEFAULT 0)
INSERT INTO t (id, name) VALUES (1, NULL)
SELECT name, score FROM t
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR DEFAULT 'NA', score NUMBER(5,3) DEFAULT 0)
CREATE TABLE src (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO src VALUES (1, NULL)
INSERT INTO t (id, name) SELECT id, name FROM src
SELECT name FROM t
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR DEFAULT 'NA', score NUMBER(5,3) DEFAULT 0)
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, NULL, 0.5)
SELECT name FROM t
CREATE TABLE t2 (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR DEFAULT 'NA')
INSERT INTO t2 (id) VALUES (7)
SELECT name FROM t2
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR DEFAULT 'NA', score NUMBER(5,3) DEFAULT 0)
CREATE TABLE src (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO src VALUES (1, NULL)
MERGE INTO t USING src ON t.id = src.id WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, name) VALUES (src.id, src.name)
SELECT name, score FROM t
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR DEFAULT 'NA', score NUMBER(5,3) DEFAULT 0)
INSERT INTO t (id) VALUES (1)
SELECT name, score FROM t
